title: The Wife of Bath's Prologue and Tale

vibeProfile.oneLine: Chaucer's five-times-married Wife of Bath makes her case for women's power.

summary: This critical edition presents one of the most famous parts of The Canterbury Tales: the Wife of Bath, five times married and gloriously unrepentant, whose long prologue is a witty, defiant argument for women's authority in marriage, followed by her tale of a knight who must learn what women truly want. With scholarly apparatus for students, it isolates the medieval literature's most vivid and debated woman, a figure feminist critics still argue over.
whyReadIt: Chaucer's most famous, most argued-over woman, in a student edition. The Wife of Bath is medieval literature's great scene-stealer.

funFacts.text: The Wife of Bath is one of the most studied characters in all of English literature.
